chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man and a woman praying at one time, the woman on the right of the man by his side. He said: 'No, unless there is between them a shibr (span) or a dhirab (cubit).'

key_terms.بِحِذَاءِ: By the side of, parallel to, or adjacent to.
key_terms.ذِرَاعٌ: A cubit, a traditional unit of length roughly from elbow to fingertip.
key_terms.شِبْرٌ: A span, the distance from the tip of the thumb to the tip of the little finger.

ai.seo_question: What is the required distance between a man and a woman praying side by side in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of congregational prayer (*Salat*) by establishing a minimum lateral separation of a span or cubit between a man and woman praying side-by-side. This ruling ensures modesty and prevents physical contact or distraction, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining distinct spatial boundaries within the domestic prayer space to preserve the validity and concentration (*khushu*) of the worship.
